summary: Sprint retrospective recorded from the actual coordination log: implementation completed, while unavailable Flask dependencies prevented runtime verification.
blockers: Flask could not be installed because package-network access was unavailable, preventing API, browser, and planned runtime acceptance verification.
decisions: Retrospective — Manager: “I unblocked backend once the schema arrived, but our initial broad tasks overlapped the architect’s detailed tasks and created duplicate tracking.”
Retrospective — Architect: “I established the Flask, SQLite, and vanilla-JavaScript boundaries, but the original task sequence did not initially make the database dependency explicit.”
Retrospective — Database: “I delivered and validated schema.sql with constraints and timestamps; db-2 then duplicated work already completed under db-1.”
Retrospective — Backend: “I implemented the API once schema.sql was available and passed syntax/schema checks, but Flask could not be installed for runtime smoke tests.”
Retrospective — Frontend: “I connected the board to the documented API and passed JavaScript syntax checks, but browser end-to-end testing remained blocked by the unavailable Flask runtime.”
Retrospective — QA: “I have no completed test result in the log because runtime acceptance testing was blocked by the missing Flask dependency.”
Retrospective — Security: “I have no completed review result in the log; a static review was requested, but no security findings were reported before the sprint closed.”
